<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, touching **10** documentable anchor(s).

**21** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 37184244b82b9e4234581b653cdc7554e74e6136`.

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `os validate (command, 81 pages)`
- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **212** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **35** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 37184244b82b9e4234581b653cdc7554e74e6136` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9a77ea3ed31a58755d68bda5dba16c9b9afb1563` — the merge of head `842ba0f7cb1392adc5de5d98af4f2cef1902864d` into base `37184244b82b9e4234581b653cdc7554e74e6136`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9a77ea3ed31a58755d68bda5dba16c9b9afb1563 && git checkout 9a77ea3ed31a58755d68bda5dba16c9b9afb1563
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 37184244b82b9e4234581b653cdc7554e74e6136 842ba0f7cb1392adc5de5d98af4f2cef1902864d && git checkout -B drift-repro 37184244b82b9e4234581b653cdc7554e74e6136 && git merge --no-ff 842ba0f7cb1392adc5de5d98af4f2cef1902864d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 37184244b82b9e4234581b653cdc7554e74e6136
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 37184244b82b9e4234581b653cdc7554e74e6136` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

**ACCEPT** at head `f6ca481e` · `Implemented-by:` `claude/issue-28505-app-package-file-install` · `Reviewed-by:` this seat (lane ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`). `Clause-②: no`. No `packages/spec` file is touched, so no `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` record is owed: the inline `spec` object is a form the `openapi` provider already accepts.

| Check | Result |
|:--|:--|
| Shape | Draft, base `main`. First line is `Fixes #28505`, the only closing keyword. |
| Scope | 6 files, +476/−0 against the merge base. Not governed (`check-governed-merges --pr 28533`). One changeset for `@objectstack/cli`. Inside the claimed surface: build route (a). |
| Measurement first | Done as the card asked, at `23d1303d`. The install-local of a built artifact answered 200 `hotLoaded:true`, then the reconcile logged ENOENT on the host path, and the instance was absent from `GET /automation/connectors`. The install caches the JSON alone, so route (b) has no root to resolve against. |
| Evidence | 2 dogfood cases go red before (the path survives in the artifact; the listing holds only the host's connectors) and green after. One ablation of `placeConnectorSpecFiles` turns exactly those red. 14 unit cases cover the refusals: absolute, escaping, missing, non-JSON, non-object. The Stripe app on `main` builds to 59.8 KB with its 46.0 KB document inline and materializes `ready` with 8 actions once installed. |
| Gates | Local: 90 derived, 90 run, 0 unrun. CI on the head is still running: 30 success, 12 skipped, 7 in progress, none red so far. |
| Artifact readers | `providerConfig.spec` of an `openapi` entry is now the document, never a path, and the artifact grows by the document's size. The cloud pipeline (#28278) reads these artifacts: it gets a note on its card. |

**Out of scope, filed:** #28534 is the runtime half of the defect: the materializer resolves an installed package's file ref against the host's root, and the dev measured it binding the host's own document. It is a child of #27293 and carries the dev's options A/B/C. #28535 is a separate defect: `os package install ./dist/objectstack.json` leaves `engines` nested, so install-local skips the ADR-0087 check. It is not epic scope and goes to triage. The dev's "noted, not filed" items are not filed: each is either a convenience gap or governed ADR wording.

**Landing:** not governed. The seat lands it (`pr_ready` + `automerge_enable`) once CI on this head is green.
